requestedActions.title: List repository names visible to the connected person, with pagination

prohibitions: Never create, edit or delete repositories
guide.summary: Forgejo documents an OAuth2 provider using the authorization code grant with PKCE and lists its endpoints. OAuth scopes are not implemented, so an OAuth token can act on behalf of the user for any action. No OAuth permission identifier applies, so the coverage uses an empty permissions list. Token-scope documentation for personal tokens is separate and not used here. Pagination is documented through page and limit parameters. Whether a documented endpoint returns all repositories visible to the connected person is not explicitly stated, so the action stays unresolved.
guide.recommendation: The requested API test is not ready yet. Resolve the access mapping for List repository names visible to the connected person, with pagination. Use “Find missing request” or add official documentation beside that action.

findings.title: Forgejo documents OAuth2 provider support with the authorization code grant and PKCE
findings.detail: Forgejo can act as an OAuth2 provider for third-party applications with user consent. It supports the Authorization Code Grant with PKCE. Endpoints include /login/oauth/authorize and /login/oauth/access_token, and the app is registered in user settings.
findings.appliesWhen: Applies when the customer's Forgejo instance uses the documented OAuth2 provider for individual customer accounts.

evidence.quote: Supported OAuth2 Grants At the moment, Forgejo only supports the Authorization Code Grant standard with additional support for the following extensions:
Authorization Endpoint /login/oauth/authorize Access Token Endpoint /login/oauth/access_token

findings.title: OAuth2 scopes are not implemented, so the token has the user's full action authority
findings.detail: Forgejo states that OAuth2 scopes are not yet implemented. OAuth2 tokens can execute any action on behalf of the user, not only Git-related actions. The token boundary is therefore the connected user's own access, and no scope narrows it.
findings.appliesWhen: Applies to OAuth2 tokens issued by the Forgejo provider for this app.

evidence.quote: OAuth2 scopes are not yet implemented.
Note Scopes are not implemented for OAuth2 tokens and they can be used to
execute any actions on behalf of the user, not just Git-related actions.

findings.title: Instance-wide OAuth apps grant administrative rights to tokens obtained through them
findings.detail: Forgejo documents that third-party applications obtaining a token for a user via an instance-wide OAuth2 application will have administrative rights. Instance-wide applications are created on the admin applications page.
findings.appliesWhen: Applies only if the OAuth2 application is created as an instance-wide provider on the customer's instance.

evidence.quote: Note Third-party applications obtaining a token for a user via such an application will have administrative rights.
Forgejo can act as an instance-wide OAuth2 provider. To achieve that, OAuth2 applications must be created on the /admin/applications page.

steps.title: Register an OAuth2 application on the customer instance
steps.detail: On the customer's Forgejo instance (instance base URL supplied by the user), register an OAuth2 application at /user/settings/applications. Choose confidential client for server-side code or public client for PKCE. Record client_id and client_secret, and set the redirect URI to the app callback. Forgejo does not implement OAuth2 scopes, so the token acts with the connected user's full authority.
steps.doneWhen: An OAuth2 application exists on the customer instance with a client_id and a registered redirect URI, and its client type is recorded.

evidence.quote: OpenID Connect (OIDC) To use the Authorization Code Grant as a third-party application, it is required to register a new application via the “Settings” ( /user/settings/applications ) section. To test
Client types Forgejo supports both confidential and public client types, as defined by RFC 6749 .
For public clients, a redirect URI of a loopback IP address such as http://127.0.0.1/ allows any port. Avoid using localhost , as recommended by RFC 8252 .

fields: INSTANCE_BASE_URL: full HTTPS origin of the customer instance, supplied by the user
CLIENT_ID: issued when the application is registered
CLIENT_SECRET: confidential clients only, shown once at registration

steps.title: Run the consent redirect and verify the callback
steps.detail: Send the user to the documented authorization endpoint with client_id, redirect_uri, response_type=code and a random state. The user must authorize the app. Verify the returned state matches before using the code. For PKCE, also send code_challenge and code_challenge_method. This is a browser step, not a curl request.
steps.doneWhen: The user has authorized the app and the callback URL contains a code and the matching state value.

evidence.quote: https://[ YOUR-FORGEJO-URL ]/login/oauth/authorize?client_id=CLIENT_ID&redirect_uri=REDIRECT_URI&response_type=code&state=STATE The CLIENT_ID can be obtained by registering an application in the settings. The STATE is a random string that will be
The user will now be asked to authorize your application. If they authorize it, the user will be redirected to the REDIRECT_URL , for example:
sent back to your application after the user authorizes. The state parameter is optional but should be used to prevent CSRF attacks.

fields: INSTANCE_BASE_URL: your full HTTPS instance URL, without a trailing slash
REDIRECT_URI: must match the registered redirect URI
STATE: random value generated by the app

steps.title: Exchange the authorization code for an access token
steps.detail: Exchange the returned code at the documented token endpoint using a POST with a JSON body containing client_id, client_secret (confidential clients) or code_verifier (PKCE), code, grant_type and redirect_uri. The grant_type constant is authorization_code. Store the returned access_token securely; this step is not executed by the agent.
steps.doneWhen: The token endpoint returns an access_token, token_type bearer and expires_in.

The REDIRECT_URI in the access_token request must match the REDIRECT_URI in the authorize request.

CLIENT_ID and CLIENT_SECRET from registration, or omit secret and send code_verifier for PKCE
RETURNED_CODE: from the callback of the consent step
REDIRECT_URI: must equal the redirect_uri used in the authorize request

steps.title: Request the first page of visible repositories
steps.detail: Call GET /api/v1/repos/search with page=1 and a limit, authenticated with the OAuth bearer token. Read the repository name from each element of the data array (the name property of each entry under $.data[]). Repositories are listed for the connected person; the documentation does not explicitly confirm full visibility, so treat the result as the search result set. This request does not create, edit or delete repositories.
steps.doneWhen: The response is HTTP 200 and the first page of repository names is recorded, along with the Link header and x-total-count when present. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.

evidence.quote: Response JSON paths for GET /api/v1/repos/search: $.data[].name (string)
Pagination The API supports pagination. The page and limit parameters are used to specify the page number and the number of items per page. As well, the Link header is
returned with the next, previous, and last page links if there are more than one page. The x-total-count is also returned to indicate the total number of items.

fields: INSTANCE_BASE_URL: your full HTTPS instance URL, without a trailing slash
ACCESS_TOKEN: from the token exchange step, placeholder only
Repository names are read from $.data[].name in the response body

steps.title: Verify the read-only boundary with a nonmutating check
steps.detail: Confirm the token cannot modify repositories by inspecting the grant and outgoing request log rather than sending a write. Do not send any POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE to repository routes. This step is a safe nonmutating inspection only.
steps.doneWhen: The developer confirms that the app code issues only GET requests to repository routes, verified in the outgoing request log.

steps.title: Request the next page of repository names
steps.detail: Repeat GET /api/v1/repos/search with the same parameters, incrementing page by one and keeping limit and q unchanged, using the same bearer token. Continue until a page returns fewer items than limit or an empty data array. The documentation provides page and limit parameters and the Link header, and the stopping condition is an empty or short final page.
steps.doneWhen: A page returns fewer items than limit or an empty data array, and all names across pages are collected. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.

blockers.title: List repository names visible to the connected person, with pagination
blockers.resolution: OAuth2 tokens are unscoped per the documented provider, so no permission identifier is selected. The search endpoint GET /api/v1/repos/search is documented with pagination via page and limit, but the documentation does not explicitly state that it returns all repositories visible to the connected person. The user repos endpoint lists repositories the user owns, which does not meet the visibility requirement.
